extraction.name: airbench (CIFAR-10 fast training methods)
extraction.description: Training methods for CIFAR-10 which reach 94% accuracy in 3.29 seconds, 95% in 10.4 seconds, and 96% in 46.3 seconds on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. The paper builds on CIFAR-10 dataset and introduces a derandomized variant of horizontal flipping augmentation (alternating flip).
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky, Vinod Nair, Geoffrey Hinton
extraction.citeAs: Krizhevsky, A., Nair, V., & Hinton, G. (2009). CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10 (Canadian Institute for Advanced Research).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data augmentation including random horizontal flipping, 2-pixel random translation with reflection padding, and (for airbench96) 12-pixel Cutout augmentation. The paper also introduces alternating flip, a derandomized variant of horizontal flipping where images are flipped in a deterministically alternating manner after the first epoch.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images normalized using CIFAR mean (0.4914, 0.4822, 0.4465) and std (0.2470, 0.2435, 0.2616). First convolutional layer initialized as a patch-whitening transformation using eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of 2x2 patches from the training distribution.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Fast training methods reduce computational cost of experiments and enable research projects requiring many trained networks (e.g., data attribution studies using millions of trained networks), making such research accessible with fewer computational resources.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The CIFAR-10 dataset contains 60,000 32x32 color images across ten classes, divided into 50,000 training images and 10,000 validation images. Used for benchmarking fast training methods.
